$comment: Shared Go/TypeScript case table for the Reference primitive, the shape of every requirement's refs[] entry. Both shipped validators read this file so the closure is enforced identically in Go and TypeScript. Each case is injected as the single entry of the document's one requirement's refs.

cases.name: a plain url
cases.why: by-locator, the commonest form in practice

cases.name: a by-name ref string
cases.why: InSpec's ref 'title' form, a citation with no locator

cases.name: ref and url together
cases.why: the branches are an anyOf, not a oneOf

cases.name: a ref array of DPMS target identifiers
cases.why: the ref-as-array form XCCDF's DPMS target identifiers reach HDF through

cases.name: a uri
cases.why: uri is accepted as a synonym of url

cases.name: a ref array item with arbitrary members
cases.why: the items of the ref array are deliberately open, so a source format's own reference record carries verbatim; closing the Reference must not close them

cases.name: a url with an undeclared member
cases.why: the Reference is CLOSED: this is the case both shipped validators accepted while the closure was written with unevaluatedProperties

cases.name: a ref with an undeclared member
cases.why: the closure holds on every branch, not only the url one

cases.name: no declared member at all
cases.why: each branch requires its own member, so an entry with none of ref, url or uri matches no branch

cases.name: an empty object
cases.why: a reference that names and locates nothing is not a reference

cases.name: a non-string url
cases.why: hoisting the members must keep each one's type

cases.name: a ref array of non-objects
cases.why: the array form's items are open, but they are objects
